items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: of course we had the old quartet which was Guerin, Tom Scott, Chuck Domanico and myself. In fact I was the leader or Tom was the leader depending upon who got the gig. So I became part of the L.A. Express.

ctx.x: So I took a lot of dictation, because he really knew a lot about what he wanted in charts. And at the end of a year he gave me “Dr. Doolittle.” He called me up in Las Vegas and he said basically, “Kellaway get your ass over here.” I said, “Okay, I’ll be right there” and came over. And he said, “In three weeks we’re going to record this music and this is your instrumentation.” He gave me the entire instrumentation, I don’t know why, and I always liked it from a challenge aspect. We had 35 pieces and a few horns…
All right. You have a copy already.

items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I got a call from a record producer I knew, Stephan Goldman, who was also Roger Kellaway’s producer

ctx.x: Were you playing tenor on this particular circumstance?

Yes I was, yes, yes. It was a tenor. And so that was ’70. So I believe the next year or I believe it was ’71, I got a call from a record producer I knew, Stephan Goldman, who was also Roger Kellaway’s producer, would I be interested — or, would I be interested, no that’s not what he said, he said, “Gerry Mulligan wants you to play on his upcoming album” which ended up being called “Age of Steam.” I said, “You’ve got to be kidding me, of course I’d be thrilled and honored.” So I go to the first rehearsal, which is…
That’s so interesting because I’ve had that circumstance in giving lessons, like let’s pick out whole notes and play — choose notes from the chord. And the student goes [scats].
